st.t: Power users: Usage volume may obscure value
st.an: The source accepts the cluster’s implementation thesis and materially develops it through concrete product mechanisms for embedding AI into repeatable, organisation-specific workflows: Workflow Builder encodes precedents and branching logic, while integrations place those processes within existing tools. Its usage counts indicate deployment and engagement, but do not establish quality, productivity or realised organisational value.
qs: Workflow Builder: Scale Your Best Legal Work  Workflow Builder marked a major step forward in helping legal teams turn their proprietary knowledge into structured, repeatable processes.
Deploy, share, and refine: Test the workflow, set permissions, share it across your team, and iterate as your needs evolve.

st.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment
st.an: Harvey accepts the cluster’s human-led workflow-redesign proposition and materially extends it with concrete product mechanisms: configurable repeatable workflows, firm-specific knowledge, embedded integrations, human verification, lawyer oversight, permissions and audit trails. Its adoption figures and capability claims are self-reported and do not independently establish general competence or realised organisational value.
qs: Workflow Builder: Scale Your Best Legal Work  Workflow Builder marked a major step forward in helping legal teams turn their proprietary knowledge into structured, repeatable processes.
As reviews come back, you can verify, flag, and discuss issues directly in context, with ownership and next steps clearly tracked.

st.t: Shared infrastructure: Harvey proposes continuous client collaboration
st.an: The source directly supports Harvey’s proposition that shared, permissioned AI infrastructure can replace fragmented client handoffs with continuous collaboration and self-service. It also explicitly retains lawyer oversight, contextual verification, review ownership and access controls, while offering company-reported adoption rather than independent evidence of transformation.
qs: Earlier this month, we launched Shared Spaces to bring all of that collaboration into one place — so firm and client teams can stay aligned, work transparently, and move faster together.
Firms can also share purpose-built Workflows and Playbooks, allowing clients to generate first drafts or access structured guidance without losing the benefit of lawyer oversight.

st.t: Vertical AI: Commercial traction cannot prove defensibility
st.an: The source supports the cluster’s account of Harvey moving beyond general assistance into embedded, configurable legal workflows and reports meaningful adoption indicators. However, its evidence is company-reported and product-focused, so it does not establish independently measured legal performance or a durable competitive moat.

kp.k: Custom workflows turn proprietary knowledge into repeatable legal processes
kp.d: Harvey reports that customers built 18,000+ custom workflows following Workflow Builder's June 2025 release. Lawyers and Innovation teams can incorporate inputs, precedents and branching logic into multi-step drafting, review and analysis processes, then test, permission, share and refine them. Frequently used pre-built workflows address translation, proofreading and transcription; Harvey presents this usage as a signal of everyday task acceleration rather than reporting measured productivity gains.
qs: Since the release in June, Harvey customers have built 18,000+ custom workflows.

Some of the most frequently used pre-built workflows include Translate Documents, Proofread for Spelling and Grammar, and Transcribe Audio to Text — a signal that teams are using Workflows to accelerate everyday legal tasks at scale.
Instead of manually stitching together steps for drafting, reviewing, or analyzing documents, lawyers and Innovation teams can create custom workflows that automate multi-step tasks end-to-end.
Customize with your firm's know-how: Add the inputs, precedent examples, and branching logic that reflect how your firm works.

kp.k: Microsoft integrations embed AI in existing legal work environments
kp.d: Harvey describes Microsoft 365 integrations as reducing tool-switching and bringing AI into email, drafting and knowledge management. It reports over 12,000 customer queries per week through the Outlook Add-In announced in August 2025. Word enhancements include table population from reference materials and prompts, organization-tailored prompt libraries and interaction history; SharePoint integration makes existing documents available for drafting and querying.
qs: In August, we announced a new Harvey for Outlook Add-In, enabling users to access Harvey functionality directly in Outlook and eliminating the need to switch between tools when managing and responding to emails.
These capabilities span analysis, communication, and matter management, and usage has grown quickly, with our customers running over 12,000 queries per week in Outlook.
Fill and Edit Tables: Use content from reference materials and natural language prompts to populate tables in Word documents.

Finally, teams can access existing files from Microsoft SharePoint directly in the Harvey platform, making winning precedents, reference documents, and existing templates easily accessible when drafting and querying.

kp.k: Agentic search combines public and proprietary legal information
kp.d: Harvey states that its November 2025 reasoning release introduced iterative searches across large document sets, with the system refining its search approach. It describes agentic search as the technical foundation for complex analysis combining public and proprietary information, including 200+ legal knowledge sources across 60+ jurisdictions, web search and internal documents. Claims of faster, more comprehensive answers are presented as product capabilities, without accompanying performance measurements.
qs: In November, we introduced Harvey's ability to conduct iterative, agentic searches across large sets of documents, refining its approach until it has surfaced the most critical, salient insights.
Agentic search also lays the technical foundation for deep analysis over multiple sources, which allows you to run complex queries and combine public and proprietary data into one analysis task.
Harvey's 200+ legal knowledge sources, including Glydendal Rettsdata, EDGAR, and sources across 60+ jurisdictions worldwide
Internal data from Vault, local file uploads, or our integrations with iManage, NetDocuments, SharePoint, and Google Drive

kp.k: Reported mobile work patterns outpace smartphone AI use
kp.d: Citing its latest study, Harvey reports that 86% of lawyers rely on mobile devices for away-from-desk work and 89% check work messages multiple times daily outside standard hours, while 75% use AI primarily on laptops or desktops and only 20% use it on smartphones. The document provides no sample size or study methodology. Harvey frames the mobile app announced in September 2025 as addressing this mismatch, offering voice prompting, automatic query refinement, camera-based document uploads, transcription and Vault access.
qs: According to our latest study, 86% of lawyers rely on mobile devices for away-from-desk work, and 89% check work messages multiple times a day outside standard hours.
But while mobile work is universal, AI access isn't: 75% of lawyers still use AI primarily on laptops or desktops, with only 20% using it on smartphones.
There is a clear gap between where work happens and where AI tools live, and in September we took a major step toward closing that gap with the announcement of the Harvey mobile app.
Use Voice to Prompt for hands-free prompting and dictation, and Magic Prompt for automatic query refinement.
Transcribe audio that can be saved as a file to Vault or used in Assistant queries.

kp.k: Shared Spaces enable client self-service with lawyer oversight
kp.d: Harvey describes Shared Spaces, launched in December 2025, as bringing firm and client collaboration into one environment. Firms can share document Vaults, Workflows and Playbooks so clients can review matter materials, obtain answers grounded in firm expertise and generate first drafts or structured guidance while retaining lawyer oversight. Guest accounts extend participation to clients who do not already use Harvey. These are stated capabilities rather than reported evidence of changes in client outcomes or firm economics.
qs: Earlier this month, we launched Shared Spaces to bring all of that collaboration into one place — so firm and client teams can stay aligned, work transparently, and move faster together.
Teams can share Vaults so clients can review key documents like diligence, contracts, and fund documents or self-serve answers grounded in the firm's expertise.
Firms can also share purpose-built Workflows and Playbooks, allowing clients to generate first drafts or access structured guidance without losing the benefit of lawyer oversight.
Guest accounts let firms collaborate with clients who aren't yet Harvey users, creating new touchpoints and extending the firm's AI leadership.

kp.k: Collaboration features retain review, accountability and access controls
kp.d: Harvey states that Shared Spaces couples AI-generated document insights with assigned follow-ups and review tasks, enabling parallel work within teams or with outside counsel. Reviews can be verified, flagged and discussed in context with ownership and next steps tracked. Granular permissions, audit trails and claimed enterprise-grade security are presented as mechanisms for controlling shared information and its use.
qs: Harvey surfaces insights across your documents, then lets you assign follow-ups and review tasks so work can move in parallel across your team or with outside counsel.
As reviews come back, you can verify, flag, and discuss issues directly in context, with ownership and next steps clearly tracked.
And with granular permissions, audit trails, and enterprise-grade security, legal teams maintain control over what they share and how it's used.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Harvey Team claims Workflow Builder lets legal teams encode proprietary knowledge into repeatable processes and automate multi-step legal tasks.
pts.d: The claimed changes include accelerating everyday tasks, streamlining contract review, creating compliance materials and client-ready work product, and promoting consistency across large matters. Lawyers and Innovation teams can supply inputs, precedents and branching logic, then test, permission, share and refine workflows. The source describes end-to-end task automation, rather than asserting that all legal work can proceed without lawyer involvement.

pts.k: Harvey Team claims Microsoft 365 integrations embed AI assistance in lawyers' existing tools, reducing switching and improving drafting, communication and knowledge access.
pts.d: The Outlook integration provides analysis, communication and matter-management functionality inside email. Word features include table population from reference materials and prompts, organization-tailored prompt libraries and interaction history. SharePoint access makes precedents, reference documents and templates available within Harvey for drafting and querying.

pts.k: Harvey Team claims iterative agentic search enables faster, more comprehensive analysis across public and proprietary sources.
pts.d: The described capability searches large document sets iteratively and refines its approach to identify salient insights. Multi-source analysis can combine Harvey's legal knowledge sources, web search and internal documents from Vault, uploads or integrations. This is a claim about retrieval and analysis capabilities, not a reported benchmark result.

pts.k: Harvey Team claims its mobile app helps close the gap between lawyers' mobile working habits and predominantly desktop-based AI use.
pts.d: The app extends Harvey to phones and tablets, with voice prompting, automatic query refinement, camera-based document scanning, audio transcription and Vault access. The claimed change is availability of AI assistance beyond the desk, rather than a measured improvement in mobile productivity.

pts.k: Harvey Team claims Shared Spaces enables centralized firm-client collaboration and client self-service while preserving lawyer oversight and sharing controls.
pts.d: Firms can share document Vaults, Workflows and Playbooks so clients can review materials, obtain answers grounded in firm expertise, generate first drafts and access guidance. Teams can assign parallel reviews and follow-ups, verify and discuss issues in context, and track ownership and next steps. Guest accounts extend collaboration to clients who do not already use Harvey. The source presents permissions, audit trails and security as controls over sharing and use.

pts.k: For 2026, Harvey Team states an intention to expand AI capabilities and improve legal teamwork and client service, without specifying measurable outcomes.
pts.d: This is a forward-looking product commitment framed around smarter work, more seamless collaboration and greater client impact. The source supplies neither a concrete 2026 release plan nor quantified predictions about productivity, staffing, pricing or market structure.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers vendor-reported adoption counts, a vendor-referenced study of lawyers' device use, and descriptions of released functionality.
pts.d: Harvey Team reports more than 18,000 custom workflows since June and over 12,000 weekly Outlook queries. It interprets popular translation, proofreading and transcription workflows as a signal of task acceleration. Its latest study reports mobile-work and AI-device-use percentages, but this document gives no sample size, methodology or fieldwork dates. The 200-plus legal sources and coverage of more than 60 jurisdictions describe available source scope. The document does not present comparative performance benchmarks, measured time savings, client outcome studies or independent security validation; the claimed benefits of reasoning, integration and collaboration are supported here primarily by product descriptions.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: Most claims concern capabilities released or announced during 2025, as reviewed on December 30, 2025; the only explicit future outlook concerns 2026.
pts.d: Workflow Builder was released in June; the Outlook add-in was announced in August; the mobile app was announced in September; iterative agentic search was introduced in November; and Shared Spaces launched earlier in December. The workflow count is cumulative since release, whereas Outlook usage is a weekly rate with no precise reporting interval stated. Claimed benefits depend on use of the relevant features, available sources and integrations. Workflow deployment includes testing and permission setting; client drafting and guidance are expressly framed as retaining lawyer oversight.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The principal affected groups are Harvey-using lawyers and legal teams, firm Innovation teams, and firms' clients and outside counsel.
pts.d: Lawyers receive workflow automation, in-application assistance, broader-source analysis and mobile access. Innovation teams can configure and distribute processes reflecting firm knowledge and standards. Firms can expose selected documents and tools to clients; clients gain review, self-service and first-draft capabilities under lawyer oversight, including through guest accounts. Teams and outside counsel can divide reviews and follow-ups. The source identifies applications across M&A, litigation, compliance and corporate governance, but does not distinguish effects by firm size or claim profession-wide employment displacement or public access-to-justice improvements.
